name: @varity-labs/mcp

tools.name: varity_search_docs
tools.description: Search the live Varity documentation for how-to guides, getting-started tutorials, deployment, supported stacks, pricing, and troubleshooting. Content is fetched from the live docs with a five-minute cache.

query.description: Search query (e.g., 'deploy a FastAPI app', 'custom domain', 'pricing')

maxResults.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 3)

tools.name: varity_cost_calculator
tools.description: Request a current deployment-price estimate from the Varity public pricing interface. Use whenever a developer asks what a Varity deployment costs. Pass `subdomain` for a live deployment's current billing projection (needs a deploy key), or `app_profile` for a pre-deploy estimate (no sign-in needed). Profiles: static-site (alias static), web-app, web-app-db, ai-agent-cpu; an unknown profile returns the current list. All amounts are USD.

app_profile.description: Pricing profile: static-site (or static), web-app, web-app-db, ai-agent-cpu. Omit for the default (web-app).

subdomain.description: A live deployment's subdomain; returns its current billing projection and overrides app_profile

tools.name: varity_balance
tools.description: Read your Varity balance in USD: available, set aside for running apps, and owed. reserved_usd is the amount set aside for the user's running apps (their monthly maximums), not a measure of funded backing. The data carries exact decimal USD strings; the message rounds to cents. Use before deploying or when asked how much balance remains. An unavailable read is never reported as zero.

tools.name: varity_doctor
tools.description: Check local-development and deployment readiness independently. Node.js and npm qualify local JavaScript tools; a verified deploy key qualifies deployment, and the report names which source supplied the key. varitykit is needed only for varity_migrate. Run this before varity_deploy to catch missing prerequisites early.

tools.name: varity_login
tools.description: Connect Varity on this computer with a browser sign-in, so deploys work. Before calling, tell the user: "I'll open a browser tab: confirm there to connect Varity." Confirming in the browser is the only step: there is no key to type or copy, and nothing needs restarting. The call waits up to 2 minutes; if it returns status "pending", relay its message to the user and call varity_login again to finish the same sign-in. On a machine without a browser it returns a link and a short code for the user to confirm on any device. Never ask the user for a key; credentials are never accepted as tool input.

tools.name: varity_logout
tools.description: Sign this computer out of Varity: the saved sign-in is revoked on Varity, so it stops working everywhere, then removed from this computer. Use only when the user asks to sign out or disconnect. A key set in the MCP server environment is not changed.

tools.name: varity_install_deps
tools.description: Install npm dependencies in a Varity project. Use after creating a project or when adding new packages.

path.description: Project directory to install dependencies in (default: current directory)

packages.description: Specific packages to install (e.g., ['axios', 'lodash']). If omitted, runs npm install for all dependencies.

tools.name: varity_build
tools.description: Build the project for production. Auto-detects framework from package.json. Run before deploying or to verify the project compiles.

path.description: Path to the project directory (default: current directory)

tools.name: varity_open_browser
tools.description: Open a URL in the user's default browser. Use after deploying to show the live app or after starting the dev server.

url.description: URL to open in the default browser

tools.name: varity_dev_server
tools.description: Start, stop, or check the local development server. Returns the localhost URL for previewing the app.

action.description: Action to perform: start, stop, or check status of the dev server

port.description: Port to run the dev server on (default: 3000). If this port is busy, the server auto-selects the next available port and persists it to varity.config.json so future starts use the same port automatically. You can also set this explicitly (e.g. port: 3031) to always start on a specific port.

tools.name: varity_create_repo
tools.description: Create a new GitHub repository and push your local project to it. Pass the 'path' parameter with the local project directory. This creates an empty repo and pushes your actual code to GitHub. varity_deploy builds from a Git repository URL (or takes a prebuilt image), so call this before varity_deploy when you have code locally but no repository yet. Requires GitHub CLI authentication or a GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN environment variable with repository access.

path.description: Absolute path to the local project directory to push to GitHub (e.g. '/home/user/my-app'). Pushes the actual project code. Pass its returned repo_url to varity_deploy.

tools.name: varity_deploy
tools.description: Submit a Git repository, a local project folder, or a prebuilt container image to Varity's deployment owner. A folder with no public GitHub repository is uploaded to Varity directly; the code stays private. The control plane detects the framework, selects hosting, builds, and manages lifecycle state. Use this when a developer wants to deploy, publish, ship, or make their app live. If the developer wants to deploy a certified template rather than their own code, use varity_deploy_template instead. To ship new code for an app that is already deployed, push it and call varity_deploy again with the same app_name: the same owner and workload shape updates that app in place at the latest commit (varity_redeploy does not pick up new commits). For an uploaded folder, call varity_deploy again with the same path and app_name: it uploads the folder again. To stop a deployment and its billing, use varity_delete_deployment.

path.description: Absolute path to the project directory (e.g. '/home/user/my-app'). Used to read the Git `origin` remote when repo_url and image are omitted, and as the folder to upload when the project has no public GitHub repository. If omitted, the MCP server's working directory is used (which is rarely the correct project root).

source.description: Set to "upload" to upload the project folder at path directly (no GitHub needed; the code stays private). Used automatically when the folder has no Git origin remote or its repository is private.

repo_url.description: GitHub repository URL for the app (e.g. 'https://github.com/user/my-app'). If omitted, auto-detected from .git/config. Use the repo_url returned by varity_create_repo as the value here.

app_name.description: Custom app name that controls the deployment URL. A static site is served at https://varity.app/{app_name}/ and an app with a server at https://{app_name}.varity.app; the platform picks which, so read the live URL from varity_deploy_status. Must be URL-safe (lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens). If omitted, the repository or image name is used. Use a different app_name to create named environments (staging, canary, etc.).

image.description: Deploy a prebuilt Docker/OCI image directly (e.g. 'ghcr.io/you/app:latest') instead of building from source. Use when the developer has a container image rather than a repo/project. Mutually exclusive with repo_url.

port.description: Container listen port for an image deploy (default 80).

volume_size.description: Persistent volume size in GB for the app container (survives restart/redeploy). Use for stateful apps (databases, n8n, Ghost, etc.). Requires volume_path.

volume_path.description: Absolute container path to mount the persistent volume (e.g. '/data', '/home/node/.n8n'). Requires volume_size.

tools.name: varity_deploy_status
tools.description: List deployments or get status of a specific deployment. Shows the owner-scoped fields returned by the Varity public interface, including URL, status, runtime when available, and creation time. A separate HTTP probe records reachability without overwriting the owner's lifecycle status; authenticated, POST-only, or transiently unavailable apps may return a non-2xx probe. Use this when a developer asks about their deployments, wants to check status, or needs to find a deployment URL. For one deployment it also says, in plain words, the current stage and time so far while deploying, how long it took once live, and, when a build failed, the last lines of the build error (build_error.lines) so the cause can be fixed in the code.

deployment_id.description: Specific deployment ID to check (optional, omit to list recent)

path.description: Compatibility hint from older clients. Deployment state is now account-scoped through the Varity public API.

limit.description: Maximum number of deployments to return (default: 10, max: 50)

tools.name: varity_deploy_logs
tools.description: Get recent runtime logs for a deployment from the Varity public API. Use this when a developer asks for logs from a live app. If a deploy failed while building, call varity_deploy_status with the deployment: it returns the build error lines.

deployment.description: The deployment id or app name to get logs for

deployment_id.description: Same as deployment (the name varity_deploy_status uses); pass either one.

limit.description: Maximum number of log lines to return (default: 100)

tools.name: varity_delete_deployment
tools.description: Request deletion of an existing Varity deployment by id or app name. Returns as soon as the delete is accepted, usually with status deleting; it does not wait. Billing stop is proven only when varity_deploy_status shows status deleted and billing.state stopped, so poll that tool before telling the developer billing has stopped. Use this when a developer says 'stop my <name>', 'shut down my deployment', 'I'm done with <name>', 'delete <name>', or when they no longer need a running app or agent. The durable operation independently reconciles route removal, reserved hardware release, and billing stop. Use varity_deploy_status or list deployments at https://developer.store.varity.so/dashboard to confirm the deployment first if the developer is unsure.

deployment.description: The deployment id or app name (the slug in https://varity.app/<name>/), including a deployment that failed before it got a URL. Example: 'worker-bot'.

tools.name: varity_set_env
tools.description: Set environment variables (settings such as API keys) on a deployed app from the project's own .env file. Pass the app, the project folder and the setting NAMES; the values are read from the file on this computer and never go through chat. Never ask the user to type a value into chat: ask them to put it in .env. This restarts the app, and restarting holds one more month's maximum for a few minutes, then releases it, so tell the user before calling. The user is asked to confirm the names and the restart before anything is sent. Call it once; do not repeat it on a timeout (check varity_deploy_status instead).

deployment.description: The deployment id or app name to change.

path.description: Absolute path to the app's project folder (the folder that holds its .env file).

keys.description: Names of the settings to send, e.g. ["OPENAI_API_KEY"]. Names only, never values.

env_file.description: The settings file's name in the project folder (default .env; e.g. .env.production). A name, not a path. Example files such as .env.example hold names only and are refused as a value source.

confirm.description: Set to true only after the user agreed to the setting names and the restart (needed when this editor cannot ask the user itself).

tools.name: varity_domain_add
tools.description: Point the user's own domain (e.g. app.example.com or example.com) at a deployed app. Returns the exact DNS record to add at their domain registrar, in plain words. Then call varity_domain_verify.

deployment.description: The deployment id or app name.

hostname.description: The domain or subdomain, e.g. app.example.com.

tools.name: varity_domain_verify
tools.description: Check whether the DNS record for an app's custom domain is in place and whether the domain is live.

deployment.description: The deployment id or app name.

tools.name: varity_domain_remove
tools.description: Stop serving an app at its custom domain. The app keeps its Varity web address; the DNS record can then be deleted at the registrar.

deployment.description: The deployment id or app name.

tools.name: varity_redeploy
tools.description: Restart an app that is ALREADY deployed from its last successful release, at that release's saved commit and configuration. The app keeps the same deployment and URL. It does not pick up new commits: to ship new code, push it and call varity_deploy again with the same app_name. An app with no successful release cannot be restarted. Redeploy restarts dynamic and container apps only; for a static site, push the change and call varity_deploy again with the same app_name. Configure secrets through an approved secret-safe interface. To create a NEW deployment instead, use varity_deploy.

name.description: The subdomain / app name of the existing deployment to redeploy, the slug in https://varity.app/<name>/. Example: 'my-api'.

tools.name: varity_machines_list
tools.description: List the developer's Varity CPU and GPU virtual machines with their state, SSH access and billing. Set include_profiles to also get the machine profiles and OS images (profile_id, os_image) that varity_machines_create accepts: CPU profiles by default, GPU VM profiles (with GPU model, VRAM, hourly price and default_os_image) when gpu is true.

include_profiles.description: Also return the machine profile catalog.

gpu.description: With include_profiles, return GPU VM profiles instead of CPU ones.

tools.name: varity_machines_create
tools.description: Create a Varity CPU or GPU virtual machine the developer can SSH into. Requires the developer's own SSH PUBLIC key (e.g. the contents of ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub); never pass a private key. Get profile_id and os_image from varity_machines_list with include_profiles (and gpu: true for a GPU VM, then pass gpu: true here too). The machine bills hourly until varity_machines_delete.

os_image.description: OS image id offered by that profile (os-...).

ssh_public_key.description: The developer's SSH public key, e.g. 'ssh-ed25519 AAAA... user@host'.

additional_storage_gb.description: Extra disk in GB (CPU machines only).

gpu.description: Create a GPU virtual machine from a GPU VM profile.

idempotency_key.description: Reuse the same key to retry a create without creating a second machine.

tools.name: varity_machines_delete
tools.description: Delete a Varity CPU or GPU virtual machine by id and wait (up to 10 minutes) until its billing reads stopped.

idempotency_key.description: Reuse the same key to retry a delete safely.

tools.name: varity_list_templates
tools.description: List the certified Varity deploy templates from the gateway-owned catalog. Use this before deploying a template.

tools.name: varity_template_info
tools.description: Show full details for a certified Varity template: required env, resources, access mode, hardware profile, and certification state.

tools.name: varity_deploy_template
tools.description: Deploy a public certified Varity template. Call varity_template_info first: if it lists required env vars, ask the user to put them in a .env file in their project folder and pass that folder as path (values never go through chat). Private templates are refused.

name.description: Memorable deployment name. Defaults to <template>-derived name if omitted.

path.description: Absolute path to the project folder whose .env file holds the template's required settings (only for templates that need them).

env_file.description: The settings file's name in that folder (default .env). Values are read on this computer and never go through chat.

confirm.description: Set to true only after the user agreed to send the listed setting names (needed when this editor cannot ask the user itself).

tools.name: varity_list_agents
tools.description: Backward-compatible alias for varity_list_templates. Returns the gateway-owned certified template catalog, not a hardcoded MCP list.

tools.name: varity_agent_info
tools.description: Backward-compatible alias for varity_template_info. Pass a certified template ID from varity_list_templates.

tools.name: varity_deploy_agent
tools.description: Backward-compatible alias for varity_deploy_template. Deploys only public certified templates with no required environment variables; private or secret-bearing templates are refused.

name.description: Memorable deployment name. Defaults to <template>-derived name if omitted.

tools.name: varity_migrate
tools.description: Clone a GitHub repository into a disposable directory and preview the transformations the current varitykit migration owner would apply. This tool does not mutate the source repository or deploy. Applying a migration requires a user-controlled local checkout so the transformed source can be reviewed, committed, and pushed before deployment.

github_url.description: GitHub repository URL to inspect, for example https://github.com/user/app.

dry_run.description: Must remain true. URL-based migration is preview-only until transformed-source custody is explicit.
